package_info.package_versions: Versions affected by SunBurst attack (late 2019–2020, e.g., 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2, 2020.2 HF 1)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion update was maliciously modified to include the SunBurst backdoor, which enabled persistent, covert remote access to customer environments. The backdoor allowed attackers to exfiltrate sensitive data, execute arbitrary commands, and facilitate further intrusions. The malicious code was signed and distributed as part of a trusted software update, making detection extremely difficult and enabling a widespread supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At service startup (import-time) and periodically at runtime (scheduled beaconing)
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (maliciously modified DLL in Orion update package)
required_permissions: filesystem (read/write for command execution and data exfiltration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup and on a randomized schedule, the code checks for a suitable environment to avoid sandboxes, delays execution to evade detection, then sends system information to the hardcoded C2 domain avsvmcloud.com. If a command is received from the C2, it executes the command locally and exfiltrates the output back to the attacker, enabling covert remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces covert outbound network communications to an external, hardcoded domain, employs randomized delays to evade automated analysis, and enables remote command execution and data exfiltration. These behaviors are characteristic of advanced backdoors and are not present in legitimate Orion software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate SolarWinds Orion DLLs should not contain logic for contacting undocumented external domains, executing arbitrary remote commands, or exfiltrating data. Such actions are not required for normal network monitoring or management operations and violate the trust model of signed software updates.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While some network management tools may contact cloud APIs, they do so only to trusted, documented endpoints and never to arbitrary domains for remote command execution or data exfiltration.
key_indicators: Presence of hardcoded C2 domain (avsvmcloud.com) in DLL
Randomized sleep/delay logic before network activity
Environment checks to detect and evade sandboxes or analysis environments
Remote command execution capability embedded in monitoring software
Exfiltration of command output or system data to external infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the Orion update and signed with SolarWinds' legitimate certificate.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of the compromised update to customer environments

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised update, causing the malicious DLL to be loaded into their environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on customer systems under the guise of legitimate software

attack_chain.action: Malicious code performs environment checks, delays execution, and beacons system information to the C2 domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of a covert command-and-control (C2) channel

attack_chain.action: Upon receiving commands from the C2, the malware executes them and exfiltrates sensitive data to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft, remote control, and potential lateral movement within the victim's network

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com or other known SunBurst C2 domains
Randomized sleep or delay logic observed in DLL execution flow
Environment checks within DLLs to detect sandboxes or analysis environments
Presence of remote command execution functionality within Orion service processes
file_indicators: Modified SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected code sections
Unauthorized changes to signed DLLs in the Orion installation directory
Presence of unknown or suspicious DLLs loaded by Orion services (e.g., with altered hashes or digital signatures)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS connections from Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Beaconing patterns with randomized intervals to external domains
Connections to domains or IPs associated with SunBurst C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion server processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to avsvmcloud.com or other known SunBurst C2 domains. Implement file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to signed DLLs in the Orion installation directory. Analyze loaded DLLs for suspicious logic such as randomized delays, environment checks, and embedded remote command execution. Correlate findings with threat intelligence on known SunBurst indicators of compromise (IOCs) to identify affected systems.
